body:
## Problem Statement

meta-skill 在已有代码项目中，容易把从代码逆推的产品概念直接当作下游需求与验收基准，形成“从实现推断意图，再用该意图证明实现正确”的循环。用户真正的产品思维、遗漏的需求、对历史决策的修正以及希望删除的产品意图无法充分进入流程。

与此同时，用户只是增加功能时，不应被迫重新定义整个产品。统一入口必须区分任务目标，不能因为检测到代码或缺少产品文档就强制执行全量逆推。

代码持续变化后，代码事实文档、已确认产品基准、工作流与验收证据还可能相互脱节。系统既不能忽略变化，也不能把“代码已经这样改了”自动解释为“用户同意需求这样改”。

## Solution

保留 bootstrap 作为统一入口，按用户目标选择路径，并建立受影响范围内的文档与证据同步机制。

- **产品梳理或重塑**：代码与现有资料 → 有证据和不确定性标注的产品意图初稿 → 用户逐主题确认、补充、调整、删除 → 冻结产品基准 → 以新基准进入完整且适合该项目的产品、体验、技术、实施与验收流程。
- **新增功能或局部修改**：明确本次需求 → 读取相关代码与已有基准 → 必要的局部澄清与影响分析 → 生成对应工作流。缺文档不自动升级为全量产品逆推。
- **新建产品**：从用户意图建立产品基准，然后进入相同的下游流程。

已有实现是现状证据及可复用资产，不是产品方向的默认权威。代码事实可以更新；已确认产品决定只能依据用户决定修改。后续实现与再次 bootstrap／续跑均维护相关文档和证据，不要求每次改代码都重新 bootstrap。

## User Stories

1. As a project owner, I want bootstrap to remain the single entry point, so that I do not need to choose a new command for each kind of task.
2. As a project owner, I want task routing to follow my stated goal, so that existing code does not automatically trigger full product reconstruction.
3. As a product owner, I want code-derived product intent presented as a draft, so that I can challenge it before it becomes authoritative.
4. As a product owner, I want the draft to describe users, situations, problems, value propositions, business loops and tradeoffs, so that I can discuss the product rather than merely review a feature inventory.
5. As a product owner, I want observed facts separated from inferred intent and unknowns, so that I know what the evidence does and does not establish.
6. As a product owner, I want evidence and uncertainty attached to inferred claims, so that I can correct weak or misleading conclusions.
7. As a product owner, I want to confirm an inferred intention, so that useful existing decisions can be retained explicitly.
8. As a product owner, I want to add intentions absent from the code, so that unmet needs can shape the future product.
9. As a product owner, I want to adjust inferred intentions, so that historical implementation choices do not constrain the desired direction.
10. As a product owner, I want to remove intentions from the proposed product baseline, so that unwanted capabilities are not silently retained as requirements.
11. As a project owner, I want removing a product intention during discussion to leave source code untouched, so that implementation changes remain deliberate and scoped.
12. As a product owner, I want contradictions and missing product questions raised proactively, so that the discussion does not depend on me spotting every omission.
13. As a product owner, I want focused discussion by topic, so that I can make meaningful decisions without completing a generic exhaustive questionnaire.
14. As a product owner, I want unresolved questions to remain unresolved, so that silence or interruption is never mistaken for approval.
15. As a returning user, I want confirmed decisions and their reasons preserved across sessions, so that I do not repeat completed discussions.
16. As a product owner, I want downstream design and acceptance to use the confirmed baseline, so that the workflow builds the desired product rather than rationalizing the old one.
17. As a feature requester, I want a new feature scoped against relevant code and product decisions, so that a local change does not restart whole-product discovery.
18. As a feature requester, I want missing documentation handled with local analysis and necessary questions, so that documentation gaps do not force an unrelated full redesign.
19. As a new-product owner, I want to establish intent without a code-reconstruction phase, so that new projects enter the same downstream process naturally.
20. As a developer, I want affected documentation identified before implementation, so that synchronization is part of the task rather than an afterthought.
21. As a developer, I want implementation facts and verification evidence updated after a change, so that the documentation describes the delivered state.
22. As a product owner, I want changed product behavior grounded in my recorded decisions, so that implementation cannot silently rewrite requirements.
23. As a maintainer, I want the next bootstrap or resume to detect changes made outside the workflow, so that external edits do not leave stale documents and acceptance results unnoticed.
24. As a maintainer, I want fact-only changes distinguished from product conflicts, so that harmless implementation updates do not cause unnecessary product interviews.
25. As a product owner, I want to choose whether to accept an external behavior change or restore the intended behavior, so that the confirmed baseline remains authoritative.
26. As a maintainer, I want only affected tasks, documents and evidence invalidated, so that unrelated completed work remains reusable.
27. As a maintainer, I want documents and evidence tied to code and baseline versions, so that I can determine whether an earlier result still applies.
28. As a workflow user, I want code, documentation and acceptance mismatches to prevent false completion, so that a completed task represents a coherent delivery.
29. As an unattended-run user, I want necessary product decisions handled before autonomous execution, so that execution does not introduce surprise interviews or invent answers.
30. As a Claude or Codex user, I want the same routing, confirmation and synchronization semantics, so that changing platforms does not change product authority.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Single entry, goal-based routing.** Bootstrap owns task capture and routing. Product reconstruction is selected for product梳理／重塑, not automatically for every existing repository. New-product and local-change paths converge on the same downstream contracts without imposing identical node graphs.
- **Responsibility boundaries.** The reverse-concept Capability and Codex product-inference guidance produce evidence-backed facts and provisional intent. Bootstrap hosts interactive decisions. Product-concept integrates confirmed intent. The decision journal records decisions and reasons. Workflow generation, reconciliation and validators consume the resulting versioned contracts.
- **Authority distinction.** Represent code facts, inferred claims and user-confirmed decisions separately. An inferred claim being high-confidence or supported by many source references never constitutes user confirmation. User-added intent is grounded in the user's decision and need not have implementation evidence.
- **Confirmation contract.** Give intent items stable identities and retain provenance, uncertainty, disposition, user decision, reason and confirmation metadata. Distinguish pending, confirmed, superseded and removed intentions. Preserve previous revisions rather than erasing the rationale for a change. This describes required semantics, not a mandate to add a second independent document system.
- **Four supported operations.** Confirmation preserves an intention; supplementation introduces one; adjustment replaces its desired meaning with recorded lineage; deletion removes it from the desired product baseline while preserving the historical record. None of these discussion operations authorizes immediate product-code mutation.
- **Scope of unresolved items.** Before freezing a product baseline, explicitly decide its scope. Unresolved items cannot be promoted to confirmed intent. Work depending on an unresolved decision cannot be declared executable; unrelated work is not invalidated solely by that question. Excluding a topic from scope must itself be explicit, not inferred from silence.
- **No automatic adoption of old baselines.** The existence of a legacy concept artifact without confirmation provenance is not sufficient proof of product approval. Reuse existing recorded decisions when supported; request only the missing, relevant confirmation. Do not silently rewrite legacy artifacts or require a full interview for a local feature.
- **Complete workflow after confirmation.** In the product-reconstruction path, generate the applicable full downstream process against the revised baseline. Preserve free planning and platform/domain suppress rules rather than injecting a fixed universal list of nodes. “Complete process” does not mean every available Capability must run.
- **Three documentation classes.** Maintain distinct authority for implementation facts, confirmed product decisions, and execution contracts such as workflow and Node-specs. Derived fact documents may change with verified code observations; product baselines change only through recorded user decisions; affected execution contracts are reconciled to those inputs.
- **Version and freshness contract.** Record the source revision or content snapshot, confirmed-baseline revision and relevant input dependencies used by generated documents and acceptance evidence. Distinguish different uncommitted source states; a commit plus a dirty boolean is insufficient. Do not use file existence or modification time alone as evidence of current acceptance.
- **In-workflow synchronization.** Identify impacted documents and verification responsibilities during planning. After implementation, update observed interfaces, implementation state, relevant task outcomes and verification evidence. Apply product-baseline changes only when already authorized by the recorded decision. A node cannot be completed while its required documentation or evidence remains inconsistent with its delivered change.
- **Out-of-workflow reconciliation.** At bootstrap or resume, compare current inputs with the last recorded state. Update implementation facts for verified implementation-only changes. For changed product behavior or ambiguous impact, report the conflict without adopting a new desired behavior. The user decides whether to revise the baseline or repair implementation in the interactive phase.
- **Incremental impact.** Reconcile affected documents, node dependencies, Node-specs and acceptance conditions, invalidate the associated stale evidence, and preserve unaffected results with their provenance. Missing information is reported as uncertain impact, not silently treated as no impact or a reason to rebuild everything.
- **Autonomous boundary.** Honor ADR-0001: user product decisions are collected in the interactive bootstrap phase and supplied as decision inputs. Do not add product interviews inside unattended execution or redesign the existing human-approval machinery. Unattended execution must report an unresolved prerequisite and refuse affected work rather than fabricate confirmation; resolution returns to the interactive entry.
- **Cross-platform parity.** Shared conceptual contracts and validators define behavior for both adapters. Codex must not acquire a different product-planning philosophy. Existing visual-review and artifact-authority decisions remain unchanged.

## Testing Decisions

- The user confirmed one primary high-level seam: observable bootstrap／resume inputs and outputs. Feed repository fixtures, previous artifacts and scripted user responses; inspect the resulting product baseline, workflow, synchronized documents, evidence freshness and execution readiness. Avoid adding separate low-level testing frameworks.
- Test external behavior, not wording or internal helper layout. Prompt text containing a rule does not prove the workflow honors it. Combine deterministic contract checks with scenario-based execution of the interaction and planning protocol.
- Reuse existing bootstrap validation, workflow reconciliation, artifact-completion checks, unattended-readiness tests and existing representative project fixtures. Test the reverse-concept and product-inference responsibilities through their output and consumption at this seam.
- **Reconstruction scenario:** an inferred user, business rule and value proposition are presented as provisional; scripted confirmation, addition, adjustment and deletion produce the expected confirmed baseline. A new need without code evidence remains valid user intent. Discussion does not mutate product code.
- **Uncertainty scenario:** conflicting or insufficient evidence stays provisional; interruption and absent answers do not create approvals. A resumed session preserves prior decisions and only asks unresolved or newly affected questions.
- **Routing scenarios:** a feature request with existing product documents, a feature request without them, and a new-product request follow their appropriate paths. Neither repository presence nor a missing concept file alone triggers full reconstruction.
- **Planning scenario:** the resulting workflow and acceptance criteria reflect the confirmed desired product, including additions and removals, rather than mirroring the existing feature set. Appropriate suppress rules and free node planning still apply.
- **In-workflow change scenario:** changed implementation updates related fact documentation and evidence; a stale required document or mismatched baseline prevents completion. Already authorized product changes propagate without asking the same question again.
- **External-change scenarios:** implementation-only edits update facts; behavior conflicts remain pending for user resolution; neither case silently overwrites product intent. Include two different uncommitted states on the same commit.
- **Incrementality scenario:** an affected verification result becomes stale while an unrelated completed branch remains valid; resuming with unchanged inputs is idempotent and does not invent new decisions or replan everything.
- **Legacy scenario:** a code-derived old baseline without confirmation metadata cannot masquerade as approved intent, but valid recorded decisions are reused rather than discarded.
- **Platform and execution scenario:** equivalent inputs produce equivalent authority, routing and readiness outcomes on Claude and Codex. Unattended execution never prompts for or invents product decisions and never marks unresolved dependent work complete.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing, deleting or redesigning a target product while drafting or confirming product intent.
- Forcing full product reconstruction for every existing repository or small feature request.
- Replacing the free-planning workflow generator with a fixed menu of nodes or Capabilities.
- Replacing the existing decision journal, approval machinery, issue tracker, or visual-review architecture with parallel systems.
- Continuous background watching of repositories; external drift is detected at bootstrap／resume boundaries in this scope.
- Automatically accepting code behavior as a new requirement, automatically resolving product conflicts, or conducting interviews inside unattended execution.
- Rewriting every document or rerunning every verification after an unrelated code change.
- Implementing this feature as part of publishing this specification, changing installed local skills, or performing remote installation updates.

## Further Notes

This specification synthesizes the user's confirmed direction and subsequent clarifications. The final test boundary was explicitly confirmed before publication.

“Existing code always requires full product-intent reconstruction” was an earlier overbroad interpretation and is explicitly rejected here. Bootstrap is the common entry; the user's task determines the path.

The governing distinction is: implementation evidence describes what exists; user-confirmed product intent defines what should exist. Synchronization must preserve this distinction throughout planning, execution, verification and subsequent changes.

The review/confirmation interaction is front-loaded and compatible with ADR-0001. ADR-0002's independent visual review and single-authority UI artifacts are not changed by this specification.
title: meta-skill: 用户确认产品意图、按目标分流与代码文档增量同步
